2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule, in short, are that Officer-in-Charge of Boalia Police Station forwarded a copy of GD Entry No. 1607 dated 29-1-2003 to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Rajshahi apprising him that over the ownership of an under construction market on an area of 1650 Shahasrangsa of land forming a portion of 0.23 acre of land appertaining to plot No. 3861/3891 of RS khatian No. 321 of mouza Boalia, within Boalia Police Station a dispute arose between Shah Md Monsur (opposite party No.1) and the present petitioner Gauhar Jamil and that both the parties with their camp men being armed with deadly weapons fell upon one another on 27-1-2003 at 11-00 in the morning. Both the sides were injured and lodged cases against each other. There was an apprehension of imminent breach of peace and loss of lives. The Officer-in-Charge of the Boalia Police Station, thus urged upon the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate to initiate a proceedings under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, attach the disputed property and appoint a Receiver in respect thereof. On such proposal of the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate by his order dated 1-2-2003 initiated a proceedings being MNGR No. 273 of 2003 under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, attached the disputed property and appointed the Officer-in-Charge of Boalia Police Station Receiver in respect thereof. In the said proceedings Shah Md Monsur was shown as 1st party while Shah Gauhar Jamil Pal ash was shown as the second party. 

 6. Mr Monsur Habib, assisted by Mrs. Luthfunnessa Lucky, the learned Advocate for 1st party opposite party No.1, on the other hand, submits that the learned Sessions Judge rightly found the disputed 1650 Shahasrangsa of land in specific possession of 1st party opposite party No.1 on the basis of a decree of permanent injunction obtained by him in Title Suit No. 124 of 1992 while the remaining 0325 Shahasrangsa of land was found to be in possession of 2nd party petitioner's father Altaf Hossain who was proforma-defendant No.2 in the said suit. According to him, though a decree for permanent injunction was passed in respect of 1975 Shahasrangsa of land, there was clear finding in the judgment of the said suit that 1st party opposite party No. 1 possessed the disputed 0.1650 acre of land while 2nd party petitioners father Altaf Hossain possessed the remaining 0.0325 acre of land. He has further submitted that 1st party opposite party No. 1 got the disputed 0.1650 acre of land recorded in his name in a mutation proceedings and was also paying rent in respect of his separate possession in pursuance of the said mutated khatian. Construction was also taking place on the disputed land at the instance of 1st party opposite party No.1. According to him the judgment and order passed by the learned Sessions Judge was quite appropriate without any abuse of the process of the Court and. does not, therefore, call for any interference by this Court.
